newsitem.title: USA: Mafia's Wall Street stock fraud broken -- prosecutors.
newsitem.headline: Mafia's Wall Street stock fraud broken -- prosecutors.

text.p: An alleged Colombo crime family associate and two stockbrokers were charged with securities fraud Friday in what prosecutors described as the first Wall Street case involving the Mafia.
The scheme, dubbed a "pump and dump," had the three defendants illegally pumping up the price of stock in First Colonial Ventures, a publicly traded company with offices in Utah and California.

They then sold the inflated stock to an undercover FBI agent who led them to believe that he was going to sell the stock to other investors, federal prosecutors said. The agent was due a 25 percent kickback on the purchase of the inflated stock.

Louis Malpeso Jr., 35, of the New York City borough of Staten Island was identified as the ringleader. Working with him were Joseph DiBella and Robert Catoggio, also of Staten Island. All three men were arrested and the indictments were filed in U.S. District Court in Brooklyn.
If convicted of two charges of stock manipulation, all three men face 10 years imprisonment.

Prosecutors said both DiBella and Catoggio had come under Securities and Exchange Commission scrutiny after two companies they had worked for, Hanover Sterling and Norfolk Securities, both went out of business, stemming from questionable practices. Both men surrendered and were arraigned on $1 million secured bonds.
